title: process-flow channel model
description: A Nextflow pipeline at the level of channels: every process and operator, what each channel carries, and the settings under which each element exists and receives items. Draft 0.1, 2026-10-10. See schema/README.md for the reasoning behind each field.

form.description: full: as tools/generate.py writes it, with the per-run evidence (`runs`, `observed_in`). published: the form a pipeline ships for the Explorer (tools/publish.py), with the evidence summarised in `generated.evidence` instead. Absent means full.

pipeline.description: Which pipeline, at which revision. A model is only valid for the revision it was built from.

revision.description: Commit hash the model was built from.

nextflow_version.description: Nextflow that produced the preview DAGs. The DOT format is internal and may change between releases.

prefix.description: Leading path segments shared by every process and hidden in the viewer, e.g. ["NFCORE_FETCHNGS", "FETCHNGS"]. Empty for a flat pipeline.

sources.description: Files and DAGs the model was built from.

process_flow_version.description: The process-flow version that wrote the model.

evidence.description: How a published model was proven, in place of the per-run evidence it leaves out.

failed.description: Each failed run's settings and the error it stopped with.

fixed_args.description: Args the same in every run, e.g. to make the test profile previewable. Paths reduced to file names.

dimensions_dropped.description: Dimensions the matrix varied and showed to change nothing.

dimensions_never_varied_alone.description: Dimensions no `when` uses but no pair of runs varied alone: possibly confounded.

params_not_varied.description: Params the code tests that the matrix held fixed. Conditions are exact only with these at the test profile's values.

unsettled.description: Elements whose `when` the matrix did not settle (also marked settled: false).

disagreements.description: Element-run pairs where a `when` and the runs disagree. 0 when every `when` fits every run.

captured.description: A real run laid over the model by tools/harvest.py: which run, its settings, and how it compared with what the model expects. Edges carry its meta keys, cardinality and examples (keyed by `run`), marked harvested.

run.description: Nextflow's run name; the key of this run's examples.

settings.description: Every dimension's value in this run, read from its params.

check.description: Processes expected under the run's settings against those wired and run; with the preview DAGs, every node and edge of the run's DAG against the model's elements. Differences mean the model is stale or wrong for this run. held_args_changed: args every preview held that this run sets differently; explained: differing elements, grouped into connected pieces, put down to the changed arg a piece names; unexplained: the rest.

tasks_per_process.description: Process id -> tasks it ran in this run.

starved.description: Processes wired in the run's DAG that ran no task: they received nothing.

dimensions.description: The settings that branch the graph. Predicates refer to these by id and to nothing else.

routes.description: The dimension whose values are drawn as metro lines, and their colours. Optional: without it the viewer colours by category only.

palette.description: Category to colour, for branches that keep their own colour whatever route is selected (QC, reporting, inputs).

lanes.description: Plumbing that is folded to one edge per process by default, such as versions collection.

id.description: "main" is reserved for ordinary data flow and is never folded.

hub.description: Node id the lane converges on. Kept when the lane is folded.

target.description: Node id the hub feeds, e.g. the MultiQC process.

mode.description: How the viewer shows the lane on first load.

detected.description: True when found by fan-in heuristics rather than declared.

groups.description: Optional labels and notes for workflows and subworkflows. Membership comes from each node's path; this only decorates it.

runs.description: The preview matrix: one entry per -preview run. This is the evidence behind every derived `when`.

path.description: Workflow nesting, outermost first, as Nextflow prints it split on ':'. For a process the last segment is the process name.

source.description: Where in the pipeline source this element is written, as file:line or file:line-line, relative to the repo root.

param.description: The param this reads. Null for a derived dimension.

derived_from.description: For a derived dimension, how it follows from params, in words or as the source expression.

kind.description: enum: one of a set. ordinal: an enum whose values are ordered, so a predicate can say 'at least'. boolean: a flag. presence: a path or string param that is either set or not.

values.description: Required for enum and ordinal, in order for ordinal. Omitted for boolean and presence.

implies.description: What setting this dimension explicitly implies about the others, e.g. choosing an aligner implies the reads entry. Evaluation only considers combinations of the unset dimensions consistent with it. Not chained: a dimension implied this way does not bring in its own `implies`.

source.description: Where the dimension's value is read, e.g. nextflow_schema.json or a dispatch in main.nf.

list_value.description: For one value of a comma-separated list param (nf-core's --tools a,b): this boolean dimension is whether the list includes it. Its param is the list.

group.description: The section of the pipeline's schema the param belongs to (e.g. 'Read trimming options'); the viewer groups its filters by it.

condition.description: A constraint on one dimension. A list means 'one of'. A scalar means 'equals'. {min}/{max} apply to ordinal dimensions. {present} applies to presence dimensions.

dataClause.description: A condition on the items themselves, not on settings, e.g. 'the sample has an Aspera link'. The viewer cannot filter on it; it marks the element as 'may receive items'.

expr.description: As written in the closure, e.g. meta.fastq_aspera.

text.description: In words, for the detail panel.

predicate.description: All parts are ANDed. An empty or absent predicate always holds. `params` constrains dimensions; `any` is an OR of alternatives; `not` negates; `data` adds conditions on the items (only meaningful in flows_when).

provenance.description: Where a value came from. The viewer shows it; the coverage report counts it.
provenance.$comment: preview: from comparing preview DAGs. source: read from the code (its if blocks, evaluated for each setting; tools/graph_conditions.py), less sure than preview. inferred: from neighbouring shapes through a shape-preserving operator. declared: from a module's input/output declarations. evaluated: from running a branch/filter closure against stand-in values. harvested: from a completed run. annotated: written by hand. unknown: nobody knows yet, which is a finding.

args.description: Command-line args beyond the common ones.

settings.description: Every dimension's value in this run, defaults included, so a run can be tested against a predicate.

fingerprint.description: Identity that survives renumbering between runs and small edits to the pipeline. DOT ids (v0, v1, ...) are positional and are never used as ids. Draft: the matching algorithm is the open problem at the start of Phase 2, and this object will change with it.

type.description: Operator type, e.g. map, mix, branch.

upstream.description: Nearest named anchor upstream: a process path or channel name.

edge_label.description: Channel name on the inbound edge, where DOT gives one.

ordinal.description: Position in the operator chain between the two anchors.

example.description: What this channel held on a real run, for illustration.

n.description: Total items; items may hold fewer.

group.description: A meta key and its value for each item, so the viewer can show one item per group. Needed where items carry no meta map of their own.

run.description: Which real run these came from.

id.description: Stable id. For processes the ':'-joined path; for operators derived from the fingerprint.

kind.description: channel: a named channel variable drawn as its own node where several things read it. source: a channel factory (channel.fromList, channel.empty). input/param: a pipeline param feeding the graph. output: a published result.

path.description: For processes: the full path. For other nodes: the enclosing workflow's path.

module.description: Processes only: the module file, e.g. modules/nf-core/sratools/prefetch/main.nf.

alias_of.description: Processes only: the process name in the module when it is included under an alias.

closure.description: The closure or argument as written, where it matters.

when.description: Settings under which the element exists in the graph.

flows_when.description: Settings (and data) under which the element receives items. Absent means: whenever it exists. Replaces the prototype's starved_when.

observed_in.description: Run ids whose DAG contains this element. Empty for elements transcribed from code alone.

settled.description: false when the matrix did not settle this element's `when`: it fits every run, but no fully probed seed explains every run it appears in. Absent means settled (or not judged).

kind.description: queue: one item per unit. single: a queue of exactly one item. collected: one item holding every unit. value: a value channel, repeated for every consumer. mixed: value and queue items mixed into one queue.

per.description: For queue: the unit, e.g. sample, contrast, run accession.

text.description: Anything the kind does not say.

contents.description: What the channel carries. Every field optional: a model with no contents is still a valid filterable DAG.

shape.description: Tuple structure as it would appear in a map closure.

text.description: What the key lists cannot say, e.g. 'dropped', or keys that differ by route.

name.description: Channel name in the code, or the emit/input name at a process.

port.description: At a process boundary: the emit name or input position.

operator.description: How this edge was derived from its predecessor, as written, if by an operator.

examples.description: Keyed by example set: a route value or a run id.

settled.description: false when the matrix did not settle this element's `when`: it fits every run, but no fully probed seed explains every run it appears in. Absent means settled (or not judged).
